row.evidence: Okta's Coupa setup points the API Endpoint at https://your-instance-name.coupahost.com/api and Coupa's Okta provisioning guide uses an OAuth client with core.user.read and core.user.write scopes; Coupa's developer docs document no SCIM endpoint, and Microsoft says provisioning into Coupa is a manual task.
row.notes: Status changed from partial (pilot draft) to none under the post-pilot rule for provisioning without SCIM: Okta's OIN app provisions Coupa through Coupa's proprietary Core REST API (https://{instance}.coupahost.com/api) with OAuth 2.0, not through a SCIM endpoint, so row.api_provisioning is true and idp.okta is api_connector. No Coupa page says SCIM is not offered; none rests on absence, with the developer sitemap (603 pages, none mentioning SCIM), the API reference, the Compass help pages and the pricing URL checked (medium confidence). No public price list: coupa.com/pricing does not show a price page (it redirected to the homepage during the pilot and returns a Cloudflare challenge now) and buying goes through a sales contact form, so no plan, price or tier gate can be recorded. Microsoft Entra's gallery app is SSO-only with manual provisioning; SAML is authentication-only (no JIT). HR systems can sync users through Coupa's Users API or SFTP CSV import. The Entra tutorial lists a 'Coupa single sign-on (SSO) enabled subscription' as a prerequisite, which hints SSO is subscription-dependent but is not a Coupa source. New row (no June status).

limitations.text: Coupa's own Okta provisioning guide points Okta at the proprietary Core REST API (https://{your-instance-name}.coupahost.com/api) with an OAuth/OIDC client, not at a SCIM endpoint; no SCIM base URL, schema or ServiceProviderConfig is documented in Coupa's public developer docs.
The person authenticating the Okta API integration must have Coupa admin credentials, otherwise a 404 is returned on redirect.
Microsoft Entra gallery app does not provision; Microsoft says provisioning into Coupa is manual (or via Coupa's own tools/APIs).

endpoints.purpose: Update user (including active flag, roles, user groups, license flags)

rate_limits.text: 25 requests per second with a burst query limit of 20 calls.

limitations.text: Nothing can be deleted through the API; users are deactivated by updating them with a PUT request.
GET on a resource root returns 50 records per call; further records are paged with an offset parameter in increments of 50.
API keys are deprecated; integrations must use OAuth 2.0 / OIDC clients. Access tokens from client credentials last about 24 hours; refresh tokens expire every 90 days.
A GraphQL interface also exists alongside REST.

okta.notes: Okta's catalogue page marks SAML, SWA and SCIM plus Create, Update, Deactivate and Sync Password in its markup, but Okta's setup guide and Coupa's own guide connect Okta to Coupa's Core REST API with an OAuth client, not to a SCIM endpoint.

fallbacks.other_sync: HR-system user sync through Coupa's standard data interfaces (Users API or SFTP CSV Users Import); Okta lifecycle connector over the Core API

conflicts.text: Okta's catalogue page tags the Coupa app SCIM in its markup, while Okta's own setup guide sets the API Endpoint to Coupa's Core REST API and Coupa's guide sets up an OAuth client with core.user scopes for Okta provisioning.

searched: https://www.coupa.com/pricing/ (Cloudflare challenge; redirected to the homepage during the pilot)
open_questions: No public pricing or edition table: which Coupa subscriptions include SSO, API access and the Okta provisioning integration is not disclosed.

Coupa's public developer docs show no SCIM 2.0 endpoint; whether Coupa exposes a standard SCIM server (Okta's OIN page tags the app 'SCIM') is undocumented. Okta's own setup uses the Core REST API at /api.

Which Okta lifecycle operations Coupa supports is shown only by checkmarks in Okta's page markup (Create, Update, Deactivate, Sync Password checked; Group Push not checked); Coupa does not document them.
What deactivation (active=false) does to licences/seats, sessions and retained data is not documented.
Whether there is a user-event webhook (Coupa 'call outs') or an audit log API is not documented in the pages reviewed.
OneLogin catalogue pages for Coupa (onelogin.com/connector/coupanew, /coupahost) could not be loaded (bot challenge); OneLogin SSO/provisioning status unknown.
Google Workspace and JumpCloud catalogue pages document SAML SSO only; they do not state whether provisioning exists (recorded as provisioning null, row idp sso_only).
Whether the Users API's license flags (purchasing-user, expense-user, etc.) can be set by the Okta connector, and how the Okta app maps roles/content groups, is not documented by Coupa.
